name: Checked Skill Preferences are listed as Jobs on Graves
description: A grave's Job line names the skill the villager had checked as their skill preference on the Villager Details screen (the one the game itself shows as their job there), with that skill's rank: "Untrained" below 20, else "Trainee", "Adept" or "Master" by the game's own values (and "Apprentice" for a child under 14 where Children's Graves Say Apprentice or the game does it). With no preference checked the grave shows the highest skill, as before. The epitaph follows the same job. Titles still win: the Tribal Chief still gets "Wise and Beloved Chief", an Esteemed Elder "Esteemed Elder", and a child the children's epitaphs. Only graves made from now on change; for older graves, Repair Saves & Logs rewrites the grave and its Deaths log lines where the save still holds the villager's preference at death. **Needs no other patch.**
behavior_changes: The Secret City's burial writer gives a villager with a skill preference checked the grave job of that preference and that skill's value (the grave dialog draws the rank, or Apprentice, from it as for any grave); without one the best-skill routine's job and value, as stock.
The epitaph is picked from that job.
explicit_non_changes: The shared best-skill routine is not touched (its other callers, the Nursery lesson among them, are unchanged); only the burial writer's block is recoded in place, same length, no executable space claimed.

The first best-skill call is given no pointer (the routine returns the value in edx too); the gravestone's value is copied from the roster entry instead of a second identical call; the chief and cause are read through ebx (the same addresses).
Titles and the children's epitaphs are chosen before the job as stock; a grave already made is never changed by the exe (Repair Saves & Logs does it where the preference at death is known).

patches.purpose: the Roster writer: age, the best-skill call 0x462460 (unchanged), then with a preference (+0xEC0 = 0..4) job = the preference and value = that skill; the elder, chief and cause bytes; the gravestone's place and its value = the roster's
